A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SUR-LID research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary materials are readable and support reliable comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original SUR-LID detection results, component ablations, replay analyses, robustness evaluations, and feature visualizations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds combined ablation, forgetting-rate, unseen-dataset, and alternative-backbone results.

M1.justification: Although the SUR-LID architecture and replay procedure remain, the stated training rule changes substantively. Equation 5 switches from different-domain positive pairs and a same-domain denominator to same-domain positive pairs and a different-domain denominator. Equation 6 changes classifier normalization to preserve the current classifier's norm. These revise the specified objective and update rule; the PDFs do not establish implementation changes or reruns.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on unseen datasets after Protocol 1 training: DFD, UniFace, SDv15, and FakeAVCeleb (Table 6). UniFace, SDv15, and FakeAVCeleb are newly evaluated. DFD already appeared in Protocol 3 but now also serves as an unseen evaluation domain.

E2.justification: The established incremental-learning comparators remain, including DMP in the relocated Protocol 3 comparison. The new backbone experiment adds comparisons against vanilla Xception and ResNet, with relative improvements explicitly reported in v3 Table 7.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce testing Protocol 1 models on unseen datasets, video-level AUC alongside frame-level AUC, forgetting rate relative to first-learned AUC, and Xception/ResNet experiments with matched replay sizes. The original protocols and stated training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a combined 'w/o All' ablation, unseen-domain generalization tests, and backbone-transfer checks (Tables 2, 6, and 7). These broaden assessment of component contributions and applicability. Existing individual ablations, MMD analysis, visualizations, replay-size sensitivity, and perturbation tests are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new forgetting-rate calculation is a performance metric, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1's AUC values and the relocated Protocol 3 results are unchanged. Added results include the combined-ablation average of 0.8217, unseen-dataset frame/video AUC averages of 0.7817/0.8258, and Xception/ResNet averages of 0.892/0.869. New Table 5 reports 3.09% average forgetting for SUR-LID, although its displayed entries average 3.76%.

T1.justification: Equation 5 substantively revises the mathematical definition of domain pairing and the denominator mask, reversing which similarities the written objective encourages. Equation 6 replaces the previous norm-scaled interpolation with normalized interpolation preserving the current parameter norm. These are non-equivalent mathematical revisions, although no new theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: aligned feature isolation through SUR and LID mitigates forgetting, accumulates forgery information, and performs well on the proposed benchmark. Added experiments provide support without redefining these main contributions.

C2.justification: The new supplement attributes unseen-dataset generalization to accumulated forgery information and extends the applicability discussion to other backbones. Earlier qualifications about weak performance with small replay buffers and limited two-dimensional toy representations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project code link in the abstract and explicitly lists each comparator's replay count in Table 1. These improve access and documentation; the PDFs alone do not verify repository availability. Existing preprocessing, hyperparameters, hardware information, and SUR pseudocode remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for FakeAVCeleb, Mnemonics Training in connection with forgetting-rate evaluation, and UniFace. The existing related-work discussion and positioning against earlier incremental forgery detectors are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Most prose remains unchanged. v3 corrects affiliation text, adds acknowledgments and funding disclosure, moves the Protocol 3 discussion into the supplement, and reorganizes supplementary sections around the added evaluations.

P2.justification: v3 retains all nine figures, with small framework-diagram edits and several relocations. Table 1 replaces the venue column with replay counts, the ablation table gains a row, and three supplementary tables are added. The Protocol 3 table moves to the supplement; the overall visual design remains.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the written training specification and adds useful unseen-dataset and backbone validation plus code-access information. These gains are tempered by errors in the new forgetting-rate analysis: Table 5's reported 3.09% average conflicts with its entries' 3.76% mean, and several entries do not match the stated ratio formula applied to Table 1. The retained main results and added validation support a limited net improvement.
